skill.name: code-review
skill.description: Review changed files for security, performance, correctness, and project-standard issues before commit or pull request review.
skill.summary: Runs a structured code review of git changes with OWASP, ORM performance, bug, and coding-standard checks.
skill.author: DavidDworetzky

security_audit.summary: Static analysis found many high-risk strings, but they occur in markdown security and ORM reference examples or in a benign local git helper script. I found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, destructive automation, or executable malware behavior in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Reference documentation contains intentionally vulnerable snippets that trigger scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the examples clearly labeled as vulnerable or safe, and consider wrapping them in documentation-only sections that marketplace scanners can distinguish from executable code.

remediation.issue: The helper script accepts a commit count without explicit numeric validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the --commits argument as a positive integer before using it in git revision syntax to improve robustness.

remediation.issue: The skill instructions mention absolute project-specific paths.
remediation.suggestion: Replace personal absolute paths with repo-relative paths or discovery steps so the skill works safely outside the original author environment.

content.value_statement: Code changes can hide security flaws, performance regressions, and project-standard violations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a structured review of modified files.
actual_capabilities: Identifies changed files using git diff workflows.
Reviews code for OWASP Top 10 security risks.
Checks SQLAlchemy usage for N+1 queries, missing indexes, and inefficient loading.
Looks for logic bugs, edge cases, and error handling problems.
Compares changed code against project coding standards when available.
Reports findings with severity and suggested fixes.
limitations: It depends on the available git diff and local repository context.
It does not replace tests, static analysis, or human approval for risky changes.
Project-specific standards may not exist in every repository.
Some findings may require domain knowledge to confirm impact.

use_cases.title: Pre-commit review
use_cases.description: Review local changes before committing to catch bugs and security issues early.

use_cases.title: Pull request preparation
use_cases.description: Check a branch for clear, actionable issues before opening or updating a pull request.

use_cases.title: Backend performance audit
use_cases.description: Inspect SQLAlchemy changes for N+1 queries, missing indexes, and inefficient database access.

prompt_templates.title: Basic changed-file review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changed files for correctness and security issues. Summarize only findings that need action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of local git changes

prompt_templates.title: Security-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my changed files for OWASP Top 10 issues. Focus on injection, access control, sensitive data exposure, and unsafe deserialization.

prompt_templates.title: Performance-focused review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my changed files for performance problems, especially SQLAlchemy N+1 queries, missing indexes, and unnecessary full-table loads.

prompt_templates.title: Full release readiness review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my branch against security, performance, logic, and project-standard criteria. Prioritize blockers first and suggest minimal fixes.

output_examples.input: Review my uncommitted changes before I commit.
output: Lists any critical security or correctness findings first.
Provides recommended improvements separately from blockers.

output_examples.input: Check this SQLAlchemy change for performance problems.
output: Suggests eager loading, batching, or indexes when applicable.
Explains why the change affects database round trips.

output_examples.input: Do an OWASP review of this pull request.
output: Checks injection, authentication, access control, XSS, and deserialization risks.
Cites affected files and lines when evidence exists.
Avoids reporting style-only feedback as security issues.

best_practices: Run the skill after tests pass so review findings focus on remaining risks.
Provide the relevant branch or diff context when reviewing committed changes.
Ask for a focused review when you care most about security, performance, or standards.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the review as a substitute for running tests or manual QA.
Do not apply suggested fixes blindly without understanding product impact.
Do not use the skill on unrelated large diffs when a focused review would be clearer.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews changed files for security vulnerabilities, performance issues, logic bugs, and project-standard violations.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on review guidance and may recommend tests, but test execution depends on the user request and environment.

faq.question: Can it review staged changes only?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for reviewing staged, unstaged, or recent committed changes with git diff commands.

faq.question: Is it only for Python projects?
faq.answer: No. It includes strong Python and SQLAlchemy guidance, but the general review process applies to other codebases too.

faq.question: Can it fix issues it finds?
faq.answer: The source instructions describe fixing critical issues, but users should confirm edits when they want changes applied.

faq.question: Why are OWASP examples included?
faq.answer: The reference file gives concrete vulnerable and secure patterns so the reviewer can recognize common security problems.
